label.verdict_reason: Loop, if/case and command-list syntax, with worked examples to look up later, not a story or design trade-off.

key_ideas.text: A while loop runs its body while its test is true (exit status 0); an until loop runs while its test is false, stopping once it becomes true.
if/elif/else tests run in order; case matches a word against a list of glob patterns in order and runs the first clause that matches.
A case clause normally ends with ;; (no fallthrough); ;& falls through to the next clause unconditionally, and ;;& falls through only if the next pattern also matches.
if and case both end with their own name spelled backwards: fi and esac.
command1 && command2 runs command2 only if command1 succeeds; command1 || command2 runs command2 only if command1 fails; both short-circuit and skip command2 when it's not needed.
A common one-line guard is [ -e "$file" ] || { echo "unable to find $file"; exit 1; }, which aborts a script early when a file it depends on is missing.

cut_request.want: AND/OR command lists, short-circuiting, and the file-exists guard idiom
cut_request.skip: while and until loop syntax, if and case statement syntax
